cards.title: An exoplanet where it rains liquid iron
cards.body: On the tidally locked exoplanet WASP-76b, daytime temperatures surge past 2,400 degrees Celsius—hot enough to vaporize metallic iron. Powerful atmospheric winds sweep this iron gas into the planet's cooler nightside, where temperatures drop to around 1,500 degrees Celsius. This dramatic cooling forces the metallic vapor to condense into heavy clouds, unleashing torrential downpours of liquid iron droplets across the planet's perpetual darkness.

sources.title: ESO Telescope Observes Exoplanet Where It Rains Iron

cards.title: Lightning strikes in reverse on Jupiter
cards.body: On Earth, lightning strikes most frequently around the equator, where intense sunlight heats the tropical ground and creates buoyant, moisture-rich updrafts. But data from NASA's Juno spacecraft revealed that Jupiter does the exact opposite. Because weak solar radiation cannot compete with the planet's own internal furnace, warm gas rises predominantly near the poles. As a result, Jupiter's violent lightning storms are heavily concentrated in its polar regions.

sources.title: NASA's Juno Solves a Nearly 40-Year-Old Jupiter Mystery

cards.title: The solar system's first confirmed interstellar visitor
cards.body: In October 2017, astronomers detected ʻOumuamua, a fast-moving object skimming through our solar system on an unbound hyperbolic path. Its extreme speed and trajectory confirmed it was the first visitor ever observed arriving from interstellar space. Highly elongated and up to ten times longer than it is wide, the rocky interloper showed non-gravitational acceleration as it left, yet completely lacked the telltale glowing dust or gas coma of an ordinary comet.

sources.title: ESO Observations Show First Interstellar Asteroid is Like Nothing Seen Before

cards.title: A miniature star system hosts seven Earth-sized worlds
cards.body: Just forty light-years away sits TRAPPIST-1, an ultracool red dwarf barely larger than Jupiter. Despite its diminutive host, the system contains the largest known family of Earth-sized planets, with seven rocky worlds packed in remarkably tight orbits. All seven circle closer to their star than Mercury is to our Sun. Crucially, three of these temperate worlds orbit within the star's habitable zone, where surface temperatures could potentially allow liquid water to exist.

sources.title: Ultracool Dwarf and the Seven Planets

cards.title: Humanity successfully altered an asteroid's orbit
cards.body: In September 2022, NASA intentionally steered the 570-kilogram DART spacecraft into Dimorphos, a small asteroid moonlet orbiting a larger rock named Didymos. The spacecraft struck at over 22,000 kilometers per hour, gouging out a massive crater and spewing thousands of tons of debris into space. The kinetic impact shortened Dimorphos's orbital period by 32 minutes—far exceeding mission targets and proving humanity can intentionally deflect a hazardous asteroid.

sources.title: ESO Telescopes Spot First Traces of Material Ejected by DART Impact

quizzes.question: Why does it rain liquid iron on the exoplanet WASP-76b?
options: Iron vapor from the scorching dayside condenses when swept to the cooler nightside
Meteor showers composed of pure iron constantly bombard the planet's upper atmosphere
Deep magma oceans erupt molten metal into low-altitude clouds
Intense solar radiation strips away the atmosphere, leaving a metallic rain behind
quizzes.explanation: WASP-76b's tidally locked dayside vaporizes iron, which winds carry to the much cooler nightside where it condenses into liquid droplets.

quizzes.question: Where does lightning strike most frequently on Jupiter, according to NASA's Juno orbiter?
quizzes.explanation: Unlike Earth's equator-heavy lightning, Jupiter's lightning is concentrated at its poles because internal heat drives atmospheric convection there.

quizzes.question: What confirmed that ʻOumuamua originated outside our solar system?
options: Its composition was entirely made of radioactive antimatter
Its high speed and hyperbolic trajectory showed it was not gravitationally bound to the Sun
It broadcast an artificial radio transmission toward Earth
It entered the solar system along Earth's exact orbital plane
quizzes.explanation: ʻOumuamua's excessive velocity and hyperbolic orbit proved it came from deep interstellar space rather than our solar system.

quizzes.question: How many Earth-sized rocky planets orbit the ultracool dwarf star TRAPPIST-1?
quizzes.explanation: TRAPPIST-1 hosts seven roughly Earth-sized rocky planets, three of which reside in the star's habitable zone.

quizzes.question: What was the primary goal of NASA's DART mission in 2022?
options: To mine rare minerals from the asteroid Dimorphos
To test whether slamming a spacecraft into an asteroid could alter its orbit
To search for microbial life beneath an asteroid's crust
To place a permanent scientific monitoring station on Didymos
quizzes.explanation: DART was a kinetic impact deflection test designed to demonstrate that intentionally crashing a probe into an asteroid changes its orbital trajectory.

guesses.prompt: On the scorched dayside of exoplanet WASP-76b, what temperature in degrees Celsius does it reach to vaporize iron?
guesses.explanation: Dayside temperatures exceed 2,400°C, extreme enough to turn elemental iron into atmospheric vapor.

guesses.prompt: How many Earth-sized planets have astronomers discovered orbiting the single dwarf star TRAPPIST-1?
guesses.explanation: Astronomers discovered seven Earth-sized rocky worlds packed tightly around TRAPPIST-1, three of them in its habitable zone.

guesses.prompt: By how many minutes did NASA's DART spacecraft shorten the orbital period of the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos?
guesses.explanation: The collision shortened Dimorphos's 11-hour-55-minute orbit around Didymos by roughly 32 minutes, far surpassing NASA's minimum target of 73 seconds.

misconceptions.claim: Planetary lightning always occurs most frequently near the equator, just as it does on Earth.
misconceptions.explanation: NASA's Juno mission showed that on Jupiter, internal heat drives convection at the poles, making polar lightning far more frequent than equatorial strikes.

misconceptions.claim: The first confirmed interstellar visitor accelerated away from the Sun without showing any visible comet tail.
misconceptions.explanation: ʻOumuamua experienced an unexplained non-gravitational push as it sped away, yet telescopes detected no visible gas or dust ejection.

misconceptions.claim: Humanity has never successfully shifted the orbital path of an asteroid in space.
misconceptions.explanation: In 2022, NASA's DART mission slammed into Dimorphos and successfully shortened its orbit by roughly 32 minutes.
